quote: The IC values of peak point C are the inputs of the base model
note: Oxford C/25 characterization charge from fully discharged state (literal P2c). Feature is a single local IC peak height (OCV-corrected using same-cycle charge+discharge), not capacity-equivalent. Current-cycle SOH: yes.

quote: S1: Complete CC-CV charging from 0% SoC to 100%.
note: tcc = time of 0.5C CC stage from 0% SoC = CC charge Ah / I (capacity-equivalent). Fig. 5a (S1 selected-feature heatmap) lists Q, (dQ/dV)max, tCC (rho 0.93 with Q) -> tCC appears in the final S1 set (figure text extraction; moderate confidence). Applies only to scenario S1; S2-S5 partial. Label = 0.5C RPT charge capacity.

quote: warping path W starts from w1=(0,0) and ends with wG=(m,n)
note: Synchronized series x_t holds target time indices g_t; last value = n = number of samples of the full 4C CC discharge 3.3->2.0 V -> encodes discharge duration = Q/I. CVs from these series are the GRU inputs. Coder's quote is motivational; the DTW construction is the real evidence.

quote: the time from 3.7 V to the end of discharge (DTEVD)
note: DTEVD/DCEVD = time/Ah from 3.7 V down to the 2.5 V cutoff under CC discharge (XJTU batch 1). Window starts mid-curve but ends AT the cutoff; authors state the 4.2-3.7 V part barely changes, so DCEVD ~ capacity minus a near-constant -> capacity-equivalent. All six HFs are BPNN inputs (6 input dims). Borderline on 'nearly full' coverage; flagged.

quote: min-max normalization is performed on the features
note: Verified in external/PINN4SOH/dataloader/dataloader.py: read_one_csv inserts 'cycle index' = arange(len(df)) then min-max (or z-score) normalizes all feature columns PER BATTERY CSV over its whole life (also 3-sigma row deletion per file); applied to test batteries too via read_all. Normalized cycle index = 2*k/N_life-1 = life fraction. Paper text alone ambiguous; code is decisive.

quote: a voltage range from 3.4 V to 4.2 V was chosen as the overall charging interval
note: Dataset 1 (proprietary): cells discharged at 3C to 2.5 V + 1 h rest, then 1C CC; 3.4 V lies below the charge start (paper notes some subintervals may be empty), so sum of subinterval times = full CC charge time = CC Ah/I. Caveat: strong only on the proprietary Dataset 1; public Cambridge dataset uses 3.7-4.2 V after 2C discharge to 3.0 V (coverage of CC start not stated).

quote: full discharge capacity curves, built from the full interval of 2 to 3.4 V
note: Ftr1 = log var, Ftr2 = log min of Q_k(V)-Q_10(V) over full 2.0-3.4 V of 4C CC discharge; min of the difference curve sits at the low-voltage end ~ Q_k - Q_10 (capacity loss) -> capacity-equivalent. Headline R2 0.962 uses full interval; partial intervals evaluated separately. SVR on 3 features (final).

quote: reaching its first peak value (denoted as F1)
note: Literal P2c only: DT peak/valley (F1,V1,V2,dV) from Oxford 1C CC charge, which starts from the discharged state; F1 occurs early in the charge. Capacity-type features (T1,Q1) deliberately limited to 3.8-4.0 V; authors describe HFs as from 'partial' curves. No capacity-equivalent feature. NARX feeds back past SOH outputs.

quote: charged capacity in time (Ah), and cell temperature
note: Sandia NMC 0-100% SOC CCCV charge; charged-Ah time series is a Bi-LSTM input. The reported 100% length case (best RMSE) contains the whole-charge Ah = capacity. For the recommended 60-100% SOC window, whether the Ah channel is re-zeroed is not stated (unknown). Random cycle-level split (within cell).

Pool also contains 'final capacity' (Group 3: directly reflects health status) and cumulative capacity -> essentially the target. 'All Feature' results in Table 3 use the full pool; the final retained subset after random elimination is not reported.

quote: charging time, discharging time, average current, coulomb count
note: Dataset B (TRI) discharged at 4C CC to 2.0 V -> discharging time = Q/I; discharge coulomb count also in pool. Final subset unknown (random feature elimination); used in 'All Feature' variant.

quote: charging time, discharging time, average current, coulomb count (during charging)
note: 'Charging time' is total charge time. TRI charging is multi-step fast charge (not Q/I). Sandia cells were cycled in 40-60%, 20-80% and 0-100% SOC ranges and the paper does not state which condition the used cells (NMC01, NCA01, LFP0x) come from, so a full CC charge from empty cannot be confirmed; it is also CC+CV total time. Charge coulomb count is already captured under P1.

quote: singular values from DTV vector and information of peaks and valleys from DTV curves
note: DTV from Oxford 1C CC charge (from discharged state), 20 s fixed sampling. FV7 = largest singular value of a k x 1 vector = its L2 norm; k grows with charge duration, so FV7 partly encodes charge time (mixed with amplitude) -> weak, not capacity-equivalent. Peak/valley features local. Task check: models trained on first 10-30% of a cell's cycles and joint SOH/RUL -> closer to prognosis than current-cycle estimation; split not stated.

quote: With the original discharge time tau preserved, both voltage and temperature profiles are interpolated
note: Scalar discharge time tau is an explicit KAN-PINN input alongside full 4C CC discharge V and T curves to 2.0 V -> tau = Q/I. Normalized cycle index also an input (P3 coded unclear; not re-checked as not 'yes').
